standards.title: Low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assemblies — Part 1: General rules
standards.scope: General rules, service conditions, construction requirements and design/routine verification for low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assemblies (panels, switchboards, distribution boards).

clauses.heading: Normal service conditions
clauses.text: Assemblies are designed for normal indoor service conditions: ambient air temperature not exceeding +40 °C with a 24-hour average not exceeding +35 °C, and not below -5 °C. Conditions outside these limits are special service conditions that must be agreed between user and manufacturer and verified.

constraints.condition: normal indoor service conditions; higher values are special service conditions requiring agreement and verification

clauses.heading: Humidity and altitude
clauses.text: Relative humidity is limited to 50 % at +40 °C (higher humidity is permitted at lower temperatures) and the installation altitude should not exceed 2 000 m for normal service; above this, derating and special agreement apply.

constraints.condition: normal service conditions; higher altitudes need dielectric and thermal derating

clauses.heading: Degree of protection
clauses.text: The degree of protection of the enclosure against access to hazardous parts, ingress of solid foreign objects and water is declared as an IP code in accordance with IS/IEC 60529.

clauses.heading: Short-circuit withstand strength
clauses.text: The assembly manufacturer states the short-circuit withstand ratings (rated short-time withstand current, rated peak withstand current or rated conditional short-circuit current) of the assembly and its circuits, and these are verified.

clauses.heading: Electrical ratings
clauses.text: The user specifies the rated voltage of the assembly and the rated current of the assembly and of each circuit; these define the verification basis for temperature rise and dielectric properties.

clauses.heading: Design verification
clauses.text: Design verification by test, comparison with a verified reference design or assessment covers temperature rise, dielectric properties, short-circuit withstand strength, effectiveness of the protective circuit and degree of protection.

clauses.heading: Routine verification
clauses.text: Each assembly undergoes routine verification of wiring, electrical operation, insulation and protective-circuit continuity before dispatch.

checklist.label: Rated voltage of the assembly
checklist.rationale: The rated voltage fixes the dielectric verification basis for the assembly.
checklist.repairTemplate: The assembly shall have a rated operational voltage of [value] V, 3-phase, 50 Hz, in accordance with {standard}.

checklist.label: Rated current of the assembly and circuits
checklist.rationale: Temperature-rise verification depends on the declared rated currents.
checklist.repairTemplate: The rated current of the assembly and of each outgoing circuit shall be stated in the schedule of quantities and verified in accordance with {standard}.

checklist.label: Short-circuit withstand rating
checklist.rationale: The prospective fault level at the point of installation determines the required short-circuit withstand strength.
checklist.repairTemplate: The assembly shall have a rated short-time withstand current of not less than [value] kA for 1 s, verified in accordance with {standard}.

checklist.label: Degree of protection (IP code)
checklist.rationale: The standard requires the enclosure's degree of protection to be declared as an IP code.
checklist.repairTemplate: The enclosure shall provide a minimum degree of protection of IP[XX] in accordance with IS/IEC 60529, as required by {standard}.

checklist.label: Design and routine verification
checklist.rationale: The standard itself obliges design and routine verification, so a silent specification still imports it; but where tests are required only vaguely, the specification should name the verification records to be furnished.
checklist.repairTemplate: Each assembly shall undergo routine verification, and design verification records shall be furnished for the offered design, in accordance with {standard}.

standards.title: Degrees of protection provided by enclosures (IP Code)
standards.scope: Classification of degrees of protection provided by enclosures of electrical equipment against access to hazardous parts, ingress of solid foreign objects and ingress of water, with the corresponding tests.

clauses.heading: Arrangement of the IP code
clauses.text: The IP code is the letters IP followed by a first characteristic numeral (0–6) for protection against solid foreign objects and access to hazardous parts and a second characteristic numeral (0–8) for protection against ingress of water.

clauses.heading: Tests for the characteristic numerals
clauses.text: Verification tests are specified for each numeral, for example dust-chamber tests for first numerals 5 and 6 and water-jet tests for second numerals 5 and 6.

standards.title: Code of practice for electrical wiring installations
standards.scope: Design, selection, erection, inspection and testing of low-voltage electrical wiring installations in buildings.

clauses.heading: Protection against overcurrent
clauses.text: Every circuit shall be protected against overload and short-circuit current by a protective device co-ordinated with the current-carrying capacity of the circuit conductors.

clauses.heading: Protective earthing and bonding
clauses.text: Protective earthing and equipotential bonding of exposed conductive parts shall be provided, with earthing arrangements designed in accordance with IS 3043.

clauses.heading: Additional protection by RCDs
clauses.text: Additional protection by residual current devices with a rated residual operating current not exceeding 30 mA is required for specified final circuits such as socket-outlet circuits; such devices conform to IS 12640 (Part 1).

clauses.heading: Selection of cables
clauses.text: Cables are selected for voltage, current-carrying capacity and installation method; PVC-insulated cables conforming to IS 694 or IS 1554 (Part 1) are commonly used.

clauses.heading: Protective devices
clauses.text: Miniature circuit-breakers used for final circuit protection conform to IS/IEC 60898-1.

clauses.heading: Inspection and testing
clauses.text: Every installation shall be inspected and tested on completion and before being energised, including continuity of protective conductors, insulation resistance, polarity and earth electrode resistance.

checklist.label: Earthing arrangement
checklist.rationale: The code requires protective earthing designed to IS 3043; the specification should state the earthing arrangement.
checklist.repairTemplate: The installation shall be earthed with a [TN-S / TT] earthing arrangement designed and tested in accordance with IS 3043 and {standard}.

checklist.label: Inspection and testing on completion
checklist.rationale: The code requires inspection and testing before energisation; the specification should require the test records.
checklist.repairTemplate: On completion, the installation shall be inspected and tested in accordance with {standard}, and the test records shall be submitted before energisation.

standards.title: Code of practice for earthing
standards.scope: Guidance on system and equipment earthing, earth electrodes, protective conductors and measurement of earth resistance for electrical installations.

clauses.heading: System earthing arrangements
clauses.text: Describes TN, TT and IT system earthing arrangements and the selection of an arrangement for an installation.

clauses.heading: Earth electrodes
clauses.text: Covers design of pipe, plate, rod and strip earth electrodes, their resistance and the influence of soil resistivity and moisture.

clauses.heading: Protective conductors and earth continuity
clauses.text: Protective conductors shall be sized to carry the prospective earth-fault current without damage and earth continuity shall be maintained across removable and hinged parts.

clauses.heading: Measurement of earth resistance
clauses.text: Earth electrode resistance and soil resistivity are measured, for example by the fall-of-potential method, and recorded.

checklist.label: Earthing arrangement
checklist.rationale: The system earthing arrangement determines protective conductor sizing and fault disconnection.
checklist.repairTemplate: The earthing arrangement shall be [TN-S / TT], designed in accordance with {standard}.

checklist.label: Target earth electrode resistance
checklist.rationale: A target earth resistance and its measurement method are needed to verify the earthing system.
checklist.repairTemplate: The combined earth electrode resistance shall not exceed [value] Ω, measured by the fall-of-potential method in accordance with {standard}.

standards.title: Plain and reinforced concrete — Code of practice
standards.scope: Design and construction of plain and reinforced concrete structures, including materials, durability, workmanship, sampling and acceptance.

clauses.heading: Environmental exposure conditions
clauses.text: The general environment to which concrete is exposed is classified as mild, moderate, severe, very severe or extreme, and the design exposure condition governs durability requirements.

clauses.heading: Minimum grade of concrete for durability
clauses.text: For reinforced concrete the minimum grade depends on exposure: mild M 20, moderate M 25, severe M 30, very severe M 35, extreme M 40.

clauses.heading: Maximum free water–cement ratio
clauses.text: Maximum free water–cement ratio for reinforced concrete: mild 0.55, moderate 0.50, severe 0.45, very severe 0.45, extreme 0.40.

clauses.heading: Minimum cement content
clauses.text: Minimum cement content for reinforced concrete: mild 300, moderate 300, severe 320, very severe 340, extreme 360 kg/m³ (adjusted for aggregate size).

constraints.condition: reinforced concrete, mild exposure, 20 mm aggregate
reinforced concrete, moderate exposure, 20 mm aggregate
reinforced concrete, severe exposure, 20 mm aggregate
reinforced concrete, very severe exposure, 20 mm aggregate
reinforced concrete, extreme exposure, 20 mm aggregate

clauses.heading: Nominal cover to meet durability requirements
clauses.text: Nominal cover to reinforcement for durability: mild 20 mm, moderate 30 mm, severe 45 mm, very severe 50 mm, extreme 75 mm (with limited reductions permitted by the table notes).

constraints.condition: mild exposure (table notes permit limited reductions)
moderate exposure (table notes permit limited reductions)
severe exposure (table notes permit limited reductions)
very severe exposure (table notes permit limited reductions)
extreme exposure (table notes permit limited reductions)

clauses.heading: Materials
clauses.text: Cement, aggregates and reinforcement shall conform to the relevant Indian Standards, for example IS 269 for ordinary Portland cement, IS 383 for aggregates and IS 1786 for high-strength deformed steel bars.

clauses.heading: Concrete mix proportioning
clauses.text: Design mixes are proportioned using an established method such as IS 10262, with the target strength derived from the characteristic strength.

clauses.heading: Sampling and strength tests
clauses.text: Compressive strength is assessed on 150 mm cubes tested at 28 days, with sampling frequency and acceptance criteria as specified; tests shall be carried out in accordance with IS 516.

standards.title: Drinking water — Specification
standards.scope: Acceptable and permissible limits for physical, chemical, toxic, radiological and bacteriological parameters of drinking water.

clauses.heading: pH value
clauses.text: pH value shall be within 6.5 to 8.5; no relaxation is allowed.

clauses.heading: Total dissolved solids
clauses.text: Acceptable limit 500 mg/L; permissible limit 2 000 mg/L only in the absence of an alternate source.

constraints.condition: acceptable limit (2 000 mg/L permissible only in the absence of an alternate source)

clauses.heading: Turbidity
clauses.text: Acceptable limit 1 NTU; permissible limit 5 NTU in the absence of an alternate source.

constraints.condition: acceptable limit (5 NTU permissible in the absence of an alternate source)

clauses.heading: Fluoride
clauses.text: Acceptable limit 1.0 mg/L; permissible limit 1.5 mg/L in the absence of an alternate source.

constraints.condition: acceptable limit (1.5 mg/L permissible in the absence of an alternate source)

clauses.heading: Nitrate
clauses.text: Nitrate (as NO3) shall not exceed 45 mg/L; no relaxation.

clauses.heading: Chloride
clauses.text: Acceptable limit 250 mg/L; permissible limit 1 000 mg/L in the absence of an alternate source.

constraints.condition: acceptable limit (1 000 mg/L permissible in the absence of an alternate source)

clauses.heading: Total hardness
clauses.text: Total hardness (as CaCO3) acceptable limit 200 mg/L; permissible limit 600 mg/L in the absence of an alternate source.

constraints.condition: acceptable limit (600 mg/L permissible in the absence of an alternate source)

clauses.heading: Arsenic
clauses.text: Arsenic (as As) acceptable limit 0.01 mg/L.

constraints.condition: acceptable limit; verify amendment status of any relaxation

clauses.heading: Bacteriological quality
clauses.text: E. coli or thermotolerant coliform bacteria shall not be detectable in any 100 mL sample.

clauses.heading: Methods of test
clauses.text: Parameters are tested by the referenced methods, chiefly the IS 3025 series for physical and chemical parameters and IS 1622 for microbiological examination.

checklist.label: Testing arrangement
checklist.rationale: Conformity to the limits is only demonstrable if sampling, laboratory and test methods are specified.
checklist.repairTemplate: Treated water shall be sampled and tested at [frequency] in an accredited laboratory using the IS 3025 series and IS 1622 methods referenced in {standard}.

source.note: Amendments have been issued to this edition; limits shown are the commonly cited acceptable limits — verify current amendment status.

standards.title: Methods of sampling and test (physical and chemical) for water and wastewater (all parts)
standards.scope: Multi-part series of sampling and physico-chemical test methods for water and wastewater.

clauses.heading: Test methods
clauses.text: Each part specifies a sampling or test method for a physical or chemical parameter of water, such as pH, turbidity, dissolved solids, hardness or fluoride.

source.note: Multi-part series; individual parts have different publication years. Year shown is nominal.

standards.title: Methods of sampling and microbiological examination of water
standards.scope: Sampling and microbiological examination procedures for water quality assessment.

clauses.heading: Sampling
clauses.text: Samples for microbiological examination are collected in sterile containers and protected from contamination during transport.

standards.title: Packaged drinking water (other than packaged natural mineral water) — Specification
standards.scope: Requirements for packaged drinking water, including quality limits, packaging, labelling and tests.

certification.scheme: BIS product certification (ISI mark) — required for packaged drinking water under food-safety regulations

clauses.heading: Requirements
clauses.text: Packaged drinking water shall meet the specified physical, chemical and microbiological limits, with testing by the IS 3025 series and IS 1622 methods.

clauses.heading: Conformity
clauses.text: Product certification with the Standard Mark is operated by BIS for packaged drinking water.

checklist.rationale: Packaged drinking water is sold under the BIS Standard Mark.
